notes.path: e4 e6
notes.text: The French Defence. Black prepares 2...d5 to challenge White's centre with pawn support, even though the c8 bishop starts behind the pawn chain.

notes.path: e4 e6 d4 d5
notes.text: The e4 pawn is attacked. White must choose between pushing 3.e5, defending with 3.Nc3 or 3.Nd2, or trading on d5.

notes.path: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5
notes.text: The Advance Variation gains space and fixes the centre. Black strikes at the base of White's pawn chain immediately with 3...c5.

notes.path: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3
notes.text: White reinforces d4 with a pawn. Black piles more pressure onto d4 with 4...Nc6 and ...Qb6.

notes.path: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6 Be2
notes.text: White prepares to castle calmly. Black trades 6...cxd4 and reroutes the g8 knight to f5 via e7 to attack d4 again.

notes.path: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6 Bd3 cxd4 cxd4
notes.text: White wants to leave d4 as a decoy. Black plays 7...Bd7 first so 8...Nxd4 does not walk into Bb5+.

notes.path: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6 a3
notes.text: White prevents ...Qb4 ideas and prepares b4. Black closes the queenside with 6...c4.

notes.path: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3
notes.text: White defends e4 actively with the knight. Black plays 3...Nf6 to attack e4 and keep the position solid and flexible.

notes.path: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5
notes.text: White pins the knight and threatens e5. Black breaks the pin cleanly with 4...Be7.

notes.path: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e5
notes.text: White pushes past to gain kingside space. Black steps back to d7 and prepares ...c5 to hit White's centre.

notes.path: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6 e5
notes.text: The Steinitz Variation closes the centre at once. Black retreats 4...Nfd7 and hits back immediately with ...c5.

notes.path: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2
notes.text: The Tarrasch Variation avoids the Winawer pin. Black strikes at the centre at once with 3...c5.

notes.path: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2 c5 exd5 exd5
notes.text: Black accepts an isolated d5 pawn in return for open lines and active piece play. Black develops ...Nc6 and ...Bd6.

notes.path: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2 c5 Ngf3
notes.text: White develops instead of taking on d5. Black trades 4...cxd4 and meets 5.exd5 with 5...Qxd5.

notes.path: e4 e6 d4 d5 exd5
notes.text: The Exchange Variation opens the e-file early. Black recaptures 3...exd5, freeing the c8 bishop.

notes.path: e4 e6 d4 d5 exd5 exd5 Nf3
notes.text: Black develops actively to fight for equal central control. Playing 4...Bd6 eyes the kingside and prepares ...Nf6 and ...O-O.

notes.path: e4 e6 d4 d5 exd5 exd5 c4
notes.text: White tries to attack d5 on the c-file. Black develops 4...Nf6 and pins with ...Bb4 after Nc3.

notes.path: e4 e6 d3
notes.text: White aims for a King's Indian Attack with Nd2, Ngf3 and g3. Black claims central space with 2...d5.

notes.path: e4 e6 d3 d5 Nd2
notes.text: Black grabs more central space before White finishes fianchettoing. Playing 3...c5 prepares ...Nc6 and easy piece play.

notes.path: e4 e6 Nf3
notes.text: White delays d4 with 2.Nf3. Black still stakes a claim in the centre with 2...d5.

notes.path: e4 e6 Nf3 d5 Nc3
notes.text: The Two Knights Attack. Black develops 3...Nf6, transposing into sound Classical lines after 4.Bg5 or 4.e5.

notes.path: e4 e6 c4
notes.text: White tries to stop ...d5 with 2.c4. Black plays 2...d5 anyway because ...exd5 opens lines for Black's pieces.
